answer: A new key gains voting weight through an auction for 72 service licenses. Each bidder burns 30 credits, locks 100 for 28 epochs, and completes two random jobs on separate days. The forge contract caps seats and rejects reused funds; a marble accumulator publishes one-use job nullifiers, while a haven registry binds each receipt to one payout key. Five of seven established auditors must reproduce both traces. Extra identities therefore pay separate burns, lock fresh capital, perform unique work, and obtain new quorums; copied proofs slash 75%, with bids and penalties public.
